name: GIS Dashboard Development
title: Custom GIS Dashboards | IoT Maps & Distributed Asset Views | Hitelecom
metaDescription: Custom GIS dashboards for distributed assets and IoT monitoring. Define map layers, location sources, event workflows and platform integration for your operation.
heroDescription: Give distributed assets and monitoring events a shared geographic context. Hitelecom scopes custom GIS dashboards around your site register, location sources and operating workflow: find the relevant point, inspect its uploaded data, review its event history and pass the record to the responsible team. An agreed Hitelecom Cloud or customer-platform integration can provide online monitoring data and configured threshold notifications. Map functions, data sources and access are defined for each project.

featureTitle:
An operational map.
With a defined data model.
featureIntro: A useful operational map connects geographic position with trustworthy records and a clear next action. Define the layers and interactions around the team using the map, from a control-room overview to a mobile site visit.

features.title: Operational asset layers
features.text: Structure facilities, equipment, monitoring points and defined operational areas as separate layers. Use stable asset identifiers so a map selection opens the correct source record and related measurements.

features.title: Coordinates and location quality
features.text: Document coordinate reference systems, location sources, update timestamps and available quality indicators. Keep surveyed positions, estimated positions and last-reported mobile locations distinguishable.

features.title: Linked measurements and history
features.text: Select a point to view available measurements, units, timestamps and historical records. Connect Hitelecom Cloud or an agreed customer source through documented identifiers and authorized interfaces.

features.title: Search, filters and map summaries
features.text: Scope asset search, status filters, layer controls and agreed geographic summaries. Define how filtering changes map symbols, lists and counts so users see the same record set across the dashboard.

features.title: Events in their geographic context
features.text: Place received threshold alarms and other agreed events at their mapped asset or location. Distinguish active, acknowledged and historical events according to the source workflow and user role.

features.title: Tracks and area-based rules
features.text: Where suitable location records exist, scope track views, zone entry/exit or proximity checks. Define location uncertainty, boundary behavior and event timing; these functions do not improve the underlying positioning accuracy.

features.title: Field and control-room workflows
features.text: Tailor map selection, detail panels and record handoff to desktop or mobile use. A mobile view can prioritize site information and inspection links rather than reproducing every control-room panel.

features.title: Deployment, licensing and access
features.text: Specify the map service, tile/data rights, hosting arrangement, authentication and permission boundaries. Agree API usage, data retention, source-code delivery and third-party costs before implementation.

planningTitle:
Start with coordinates.
Finish with clear decisions.
planningIntro: Map appearance, data interpretation and operating responsibilities should be specified together.

planning.title: Define the operating geography
planning.text: List the areas, assets and users the map must support. Review coordinates, boundary data and location quality before choosing the base map and operational layers.
planning.brief: Coverage · Coordinate reference · Asset register · Location quality · Map rights

planning.title: Define the record and event contract
planning.text: Review sample data for asset identity, measurements, timestamps, quality, event status and history. Specify missing, duplicate, delayed and out-of-order record handling.
planning.brief: API samples · Identity mapping · Time semantics · Event states · Retention

planning.title: Verify the map workflow
planning.text: Choose representative sites, events, permissions and mobile tasks. Agree how map, lists, counts and record handoff should behave with that dataset and target devices.
planning.brief: User scenarios · Layer rules · Target devices · Acceptance dataset · Handover

faqs.q: What distinguishes a GIS dashboard from a general monitoring dashboard?
faqs.a: A GIS dashboard makes geographic location and operational layers part of the investigation workflow. It connects selected assets or areas with measurements, events and source records; the map, lists and summaries should follow the same data selection.

faqs.q: Can fixed sensors and mobile assets appear on the same map?
faqs.a: They can be scoped as separate layers with their own location sources and timestamp rules. A surveyed sensor position and a last-reported mobile location should remain distinguishable to the user.

faqs.q: Does the dashboard improve positioning accuracy?
faqs.a: No. Accuracy comes from the positioning, survey or other location source. The project defines coordinate transformations and how available quality indicators, uncertainty and stale records are represented.

faqs.q: Can it use our existing map service and asset layers?
faqs.a: They can be reviewed for supported interfaces, coverage, coordinate reference systems, access control and usage rights. Map tiles, commercial services and third-party datasets retain their licence and commercial conditions.

faqs.q: Can Hitelecom Cloud data be used?
faqs.a: An agreed integration can provide uploaded monitoring data and configured threshold events from Hitelecom Cloud. Asset identity, point coordinates, channel definitions, units and timestamps are mapped to the dashboard’s layers.

faqs.q: Can the map display historical routes and condition records?
faqs.a: Where authorized history is available, a project can scope time-filtered tracks and linked measurements. Retention, clock alignment, missing records and any interpolation or aggregation rules are defined before implementation.

faqs.q: Are geofences and dwell-time calculations standard features?
faqs.a: They are project options rather than universal inclusions. Suitable position data, licensed boundaries, uncertainty handling, entry/exit rules and calculation semantics must support the intended use.

faqs.q: How are map alarms and notifications handled?
faqs.a: Events may be received from an existing monitoring platform or generated by an expressly scoped rules service. The project identifies threshold ownership, event status, notification recipients and any acknowledgement or downstream handoff.

faqs.q: Can the map work on a phone or without connectivity?
faqs.a: Mobile layouts are designed around the selected field tasks and target devices. Offline maps or cached records require a separate decision on licensing, storage, data freshness, synchronization and access security.

faqs.q: Can different customers or contractors see different sites?
faqs.a: Access can be scoped by organization, region, site or role. Test the permitted map layers, detail records, exports and source-system links with representative user accounts before acceptance.

faqs.q: What information is needed for a quotation?
faqs.a: Share the coverage area, asset register, sample coordinates, source API or record samples, map preference, user roles and desired workflows. Include expected dataset sizes, retention, target devices and the proposed deployment environment.

faqs.q: What documents and source rights are handed over?
faqs.a: The contract defines the application build, configuration, layer schema, interface mapping, acceptance records and deployment instructions to be delivered. Source-code rights, map licences, third-party costs and support responsibilities are agreed explicitly.
